items.title: [wildcard] Replace the static sendability proof with exhaustive schedule enumeration + a replayable certificate (bounded subset)

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Replace Tier-0's static sendability proof, for admitted bounded regions, with exhaustive schedule enumeration plus a replayable certificate. For a region whose task count, channel depths and data domains are finite (the admission shape already used by #378), the compiler enumerates the complete interleaving graph of the emitted Go — every spawn order, every channel send/recv pairing, every managed-hatch entry — and ships a machine-checkable certificate: no reachable state has two tasks holding an unsynchronized mutable alias. The checker stops being the authority and becomes a fast pre-filter; the authority is a bounded model-check a third party can replay in seconds. The product becomes a certificate, not a proof obligation on the reader. For regions too large to enumerate, the compiler must emit the witness schedule a human can step through, instead of an unreadable dataflow trace.

### Which assumption it breaks

Two sacred cows: (1) that Tier-0's guarantee must be a static dataflow theorem, and (2) that fail-closed is the only honest answer for an unproven value. Enumeration gives a third answer for the bounded subset: decided, with evidence. It also changes what GUARANTEES rows 1-6 mean — those rows are currently claimed on the strength of the checker's rules; here the same rows are claimed on the strength of an exhaustive reachable-state search, a strictly stronger and independently checkable claim for the admitted subset. Adjacent to W-018 (SDF certificates) and W-023 (Go toolchain as oracle), but neither enumerates interleavings: #378 certifies a schedule, #023 certifies buildability, this certifies absence of a racy reachable state.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

A normal feature bounty would reject this because it does not make the checker smarter — it makes the checker demotable. That is the point: Hybrid's value proposition is races become compile errors, and the honest way to earn that sentence is to show the state space, not to trust a rule set. It also changes what the corpus is for: today the corpus pins expected verdicts; here the corpus becomes the training set for admission bounds — every corpus program gets a certificate, and certificate size becomes the metric that separates Tier-0-certifiable programs from checker-only ones. The compiler's output contract gains a new artifact type, which is a paradigm change, not a feature.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Falsifiable three ways, all cheap: (a) Agreement — enumerate all 137 corpus programs; if enumeration disagrees with the checker on any case, that disagreement is a soundness signal and the idea is already paid for, publish it. (b) Bound — if the admitted subset covers under 60% of the corpus within a 10^7-state budget per program, the certification story is too narrow to ship and that bound is the learning. (c) Cost — certificate replay must stay under 2s per program in CI, or the third party can check it claim dies. Milestone plan: M1 = enumerator + certificate format over the existing corpus, with a disagreement report; M2 = admission-bound study + published falsifier results, success or failure.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

This does not delete the Rust checker — it demotes it to pre-filter, so two verdict sources can drift and that drift is a permanent maintenance tax. Enumerating managed blocks honestly is the hard part: a hatch is an unmodeled escape, so the certificate must either model the hatch's synchronization (mutex/atomic/actor) or exclude it and say so, which narrows the admitted subset. Expect the emit pipeline to gain a certificate sidecar and the corpus harness to gain a replay step; neither is a rewrite, but both are permanent surface area.

- [x] I understand no prototype is required and failure-with-knowledge is a valid, paid outcome
- [x] I understand all outcomes (including declines and failures) are published in MOONSHOT.md

items.title: [wildcard] Synthesize progress strategies for bounded, data-dependent task regions

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Give an opt-in, bounded Hybrid task region a compiler-synthesized **progress strategy**. The compiler explores its finite, data-dependent interaction model, distinguishes scheduling choices it may control from outcomes it must tolerate, and emits a coordinator that follows a winning reachability strategy. A region is admitted only when that strategy forces every modeled execution to a declared terminal state. The product is executable progress enforcement, with an auditable rank certificate. It keeps Tier-0 value-safety checks and changes execution semantics inside the admitted region. This addresses the explicit absence of a general liveness guarantee in [GUARANTEES.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/6d3882e250ea683b506d4c7d1ce77d416b5d2c39/GUARANTEES.md).

### Which assumption it breaks

The assumption to challenge is that concurrent execution should retain every source-legal scheduling choice once value sharing passes checking. For a declared progress region, the compiler would instead be authorized to remove **controllable scheduling choices** that obstruct completion, while preserving every allowed environment outcome. That requires a different backend for the region, initially explicit task state machines under one coordinator.

The first subset has fixed task counts, bounded FIFO channels and finite data domains; total, terminating local steps; and no foreign blocking calls, callbacks, managed escapes, dynamic spawning, cancellation or unbounded recursion. Inputs must have an explicit finite contract. These are admission conditions, not assumptions silently applied to arbitrary Go. A stalled external input remains a losing behavior unless the contract actually excludes it. The claim concerns modeled transition progress, not wall-clock deadlines.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

This changes the compiler's output contract: a concurrency design may be admitted because an enforceable strategy can make it finish, even though some otherwise legal schedules lose. The risky architectural change is granting the generated runtime that authority and validating its connection to source semantics.

Existing work deserves explicit credit. [#605](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/605) already proposes a replay coordinator for data-dependent task islands; a coordinator alone is not the contribution here. [#1962](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/1962) serializes conflicts but excludes blocking receives. [W-018/#378](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/378) uses fixed-rate dataflow schedules, while [W-010/#184](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/184) and [#1279](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/1279) start from global protocols. [W-013/#345](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/345) concerns translation validation. This proposal's specific question is whether adversarial reachability synthesis can control a useful, bounded, data-dependent source region and carry an independently checked progress strategy through execution.

The mathematical techniques are established prior art: [Ehlers, Lafortune, Tripakis and Vardi, Supervisory Control and Reactive Synthesis (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10626-015-0223-0). The proposed contribution is the Hybrid admission and execution experiment. A bounded tracker search found no identical proposal; that is not a proof of global novelty.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

**Proposed contract.** A terminal state means every admitted task has settled and the declared output/close obligations are discharged; a stuck task or timeout cannot be relabeled terminal. Partition a finite graph into controller states C, environment states E, terminal states T, and explicit failure states. Start W0 = T. Repeatedly add:

- a controller state with at least one legal successor in the previous W;
- an environment state with a **nonempty** successor set whose **every** legal successor is in the previous W.

Failure states are never added. Every nonterminal state with no successor loses, including an environment dead end. Admit an initial state only if it enters this least reachability attractor.

Assign each winning state its first-entry iteration as a natural-number rank. The runtime selects a controller edge with a strictly smaller rank; every environment edge must also decrease rank. Merely allowing every edge that remains in the winning region is insufficient: a controller self-loop could otherwise run forever. Strict descent is the finite-game progress argument. Resource exhaustion or an incomplete graph yields UNKNOWN/rejection.

**Authority boundary.** Scheduling and any source-ready select choices explicitly delegated to the coordinator can be controllable. Input values, adversarial choices and any scheduler behavior outside that authority are environment moves; they cannot be pruned or relabeled to obtain a win. A zero-capacity send/receive is one atomic paired transition, with payload and ownership effects modeled together. A coordinator cannot invent a ready operation, a value or a successful receive.

**Minimal falsifier.** Let the environment choose observable L or R. At C_L, action A reaches T and B reaches a dead end; at C_R the outcomes reverse. A reactive policy wins, while choosing the same action in both states loses. This is a graph-level discriminator, not a claimed Hybrid program or measured result. Add these negative variants before implementation:

1. Add an uncontrollable edge to a dead end: reject the initial state.
2. Add a controller self-loop alongside a successful exit: reject a certificate that permits the loop without progress.
3. Allow the environment to stutter forever: reject a completion claim without a separately justified assumption.
4. Add a nonterminal environment state with zero successors: do not accept through a vacuous universal condition.
5. Split an unbuffered handshake into independently schedulable halves: flag the incorrect model.
6. Let an emitted operation bypass the coordinator or take an unmodeled foreign call: refuse the claimed source/runtime correspondence.

**If selected, preregister a bounded spike before measurements.** First build the explicit-game solver and a separate rank/policy checker; cross-check tiny games against exhaustive strategy enumeration. Next specify source-to-game lowering for two small protocols with input-dependent choices and blocking operations, and compare generated execution traces against the independent model. Preserve all environment alternatives and show that concrete execution steps implement the modeled operations, including any bounded internal steps. A toy winning graph alone does not establish this correspondence.

An initial stop budget would be 50,000 states / 500,000 edges, 1 GiB and 30 CPU-seconds per instance. Record budget failures as failures. Compare coordinator cost, allocations and useful admitted protocols with the same bounded backend without supervision and with applicable static-order/dataflow restrictions. These are proposed experiments; no speedup, benchmark result or integration is claimed.

The idea fails if a losing behavior can escape the strategy, the required authority cannot be enforced, realistic small protocols exceed the state budget, or existing proposals already provide the same contract. Publish that boundary and its smallest counterexample as the learning.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

The solver is probably easier than the semantic boundary. This rewrites task/channel emission for the opt-in region, may sacrifice parallel throughput, and needs a checkable relationship among source, game and generated coordinator. Finite-state explosion and a tiny useful subset may make the tradeoff unattractive. The first spike excludes cancellation, foreign I/O and general Go integration; their guarantees would need separate work. Existing Tier-0 checks remain in force.

AI-assisted original design proposal. No compiler prototype, test run, measured performance, completed refinement proof or award is asserted.

items.title: [wildcard] Zero-copy loan slices across the assembly trampoline via static GC-pin certificates

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Eliminate serialization and buffer-copy overhead across the Go-to-Rust assembly trampoline (call_sysv.s / call_win64.s) by letting hy-check's existing loan checker (SPEC-LANGUAGE.md §9) issue static stack-bound pin certificates for borrowed slices (&[]byte, &string). Currently, crossing into the Rust staticlib (serde_json, regex, sha3) requires copying payload bytes or marshaling across the bridge because Go's GC moving/stack-shrinking semantics forbid raw pointer retention across arbitrary calls. However, because Hybrid's assembly trampoline executes synchronously on a switched system stack with bounded two-tier budgets (Spike 1 & Spike 4) and cannot trigger a Go stack growth on the caller frame while suspended, any non-escaping loan proven exclusive by Tier-0 can be passed as a raw {ptr, len} fat pointer directly into Rust  &[u8] with zero allocation and zero copying.

### Which assumption it breaks

Breaks the assumption in Spike 1 / G2 and SPEC-LANGUAGE.md that the Go-to-Rust staticlib bridge must treat slice/string arguments as value-copied or opaque ABI buffers to preserve Go GC invariants. It merges Tier-0 static loan lifetimes (hy-check) directly with the low-level assembly trampoline ABI (hy-emit + runtime/).

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

While Spike 1 reduced call overhead from 46.8 ns (cgo) to 3.37 ns via stack-switched assembly trampolines, that 16.5x win only applies to fixed-size scalar arguments; real-world workloads (serde_json parsing 64 KB payloads or sha3 hashing buffers) immediately lose that advantage to O(N) memory copying across the boundary. Proving that Tier-0 exclusive loans mathematically guarantee pointer stability during synchronous trampoline execution turns Hybrid's ownership checker from a purely defensive safety tool into a zero-copy performance weapon that beats handwritten cgo on throughput, not just call latency.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Falsifiable Metric: Benchmark sha3 and serde_json bridge crossings on 1 KiB, 64 KiB, and 1 MiB payloads using borrowed &[]byte fat-pointer views vs. current bridge lowering; throughput must improve by >=3x on >=64 KiB payloads with 0 B/op and 0 allocs/op under go test -bench and clean execution under -race + GODEBUG=gcstoptheworld=1 / stack-move stress tests (runtime.GC()).

Defeat Condition: If Go 1.26.9's concurrent mark/sweep or stack shrinking can relocate a stack-allocated backing array of a slice while its goroutine is parked on the assembly trampoline stack switch without runtime. Pinner overhead, or if pinning costs exceed the O(N) copy time for payloads under 16 KiB, the zero copy static loan assumption is falsified.
Settlement Wallet (Base USDC): 0xefC7eC8C30c29e2f48810A5b0AB0693DA3DFcc6e

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

Static proof holds trivially for heap-backed slices under Go's non-moving heap collector, but stack-allocated backing arrays require proving the goroutine stack cannot shrink while parked across the assembly trampoline boundary; if false, the compiler must force escape-to-heap on bridge loaned slices.

items.title: [wildcard] Certified Task-Region Memory Budgets: compile-time static max-RSS certificates

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Introduce static task memory budgeting (task(budget = 16.MiB) worker()) certified by an allocation-effect contract at compile time. Currently, Hybrid proves data-race freedom across tasks (GUARANTEES.md Row 1) and memory safety via Go's GC (Row 17), but explicitly makes zero claims about memory exhaustion (OOM), task leak budgets, or allocation bounds. By coupling the escape analysis of hy-check with an affine capability-bounded allocation budget, every spawned task carries an allocation certificate verified against its static call graph. If a task cannot be bounded, it must either be marked unbounded (task(budget = unmetered)) or routed through an isolated arena/slab allocator that fails gracefully (or cancels the task scope) instead of killing the entire Go process via OS OOM.

### Which assumption it breaks

Kills the sacred cow in GUARANTEES.md Row 17 (Memory safety, Go side: Go's GC, unchanged - Hybrid emits Go source): breaks the assumption that Go's runtime GC alone is sufficient for robust concurrent services. Extends Tier-0 to verify capacity bounds in addition to dataflow. Challenges unconstrained goroutine emission in hy-emit.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Normal feature bounties optimize existing AST lowering or catch compiler bugs in the current shape. This proposal addresses the single largest operational failure mode of concurrent Go services in production: runaway goroutines accumulating heap memory until the kernel OOM killer terminates the container. Hybrid already possesses the exact machinery needed to fix this—its linear loan checker, escape-path tracker, and composite ownership model (Section 9.3). Turning those flow proofs into an upper-bound memory certificate turns Hybrid from 'Go with data-race checks' into 'Go with mission-critical bounded execution guarantees'.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

1. Falsifiable Metric: Formulate allocation-cost model in hy-check. For streaming fan-out with 10k tasks, hyb check computes an upper-bound footprint within 15% of measured heap delta under runtime.ReadMemStats(). 2. Defeat Condition: If recursion or foreign Go calls degrade static upper bound to Infinity on >40% of non-trivial code, static approach is falsified and pivots to explicit bounded runtime arenas with ErrTaskMemoryExceeded. Settlement Wallet (Base USDC): 0x7Fc0F41448f8e6622487Bc31cAa7a692c2777a71

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

_No response_

items.title: [wildcard] Make hy-check an untrusted proof producer: permission certificates for actual Go

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

For an opt-in certified subset, make neither `hy-check` nor `hy-emit` trusted for the emitted artifact's race-freedom claim. They produce Go plus a candidate permission derivation; an independent kernel checks that derivation against the **actual typed Go CFG**, including allocations, aliases, reads/writes and spawn/send transfers. A frontend ACCEPT or a certificate merely asserting ‘sendable’ is not evidence. The research question is whether explicit proof checking can remove inference/search from the trusted safety core without becoming another full checker.

### Which assumption it breaks

Challenge trusting `hy-check`'s implementation for the certified artifact's safety. At inspected main `1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b`, [stmt.rs:39–69](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/compiler/crates/hy-emit/src/stmt.rs#L39) intentionally erases move markers and emits ordinary Go sends/goroutines. That is not a bug report. Could the resulting artifact instead carry independently checked safety evidence even when inference is wrong?

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

- [W-013/#345](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/345) explicitly **keeps hy-check trusted** and verifies checked-IR-to-Go preservation. Here the checker is also an untrusted proof producer; the target is a direct safety property of actual Go.
- [W-004/#174](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/174) relies on phantom witnesses and `cmd/compile`. This kernel would check permission/alias derivations for supported storage and reject unsupported captures; ordinary Go type-checking alone cannot certify it.
- [W-023/#565](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/565) uses toolchain/test oracles. Finitely many successful executions are not a proof derivation.

Proof-carrying code is established work, not a claimed invention here. The bounded tracker searches did not identify this same trust-boundary change; they are not an exhaustive novelty proof. If maintainers group it with an existing family, shared evaluation or decline is preferable to duplicate work.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

**Initial boundary:** a closed program with scalar inputs and internally allocated storage. Support scalars, slices of scalars with explicit backing roots, static callees, branches, and one-way spawn/send ownership transfer. Borrowed mutable entry inputs, mutable globals, loops, defer/panic/recover, closures, maps, FFI, managed code, unsafe, reflection and unresolved dispatch initially receive no certificate. Calls require a checked callee derivation in the same closed artifact.

**Obligation:** cover every actual CFG edge and memory operation. Reference copies retain their backing-root identity; only a checked allocation rule creates freshness. Write permission cannot be duplicated among concurrently live tasks. Check join assertions rather than trust them. Bind the proof to the full Go input set actually compiled, build tags/platform/toolchain configuration, checked callee derivations, semantics and kernel version.

| Proposed falsifier/control | Required outcome |
|---|---|
| Supported spawn/send with actual reads/writes and uniquely transferred storage | Accept |
| Surviving-alias writes after transfer; overlapping concurrent slice writes | Reject |
| Forged freshness/sendable labels, omitted CFG edges, unsafe type-correct output mutations | Reject independently of hy-check |
| Unsupported constructs, changed artifact, incomplete derivation | No certificate |
| Race-free but functionally wrong output | May pass safety; must still fail the separate behaviour gate |

An illustrative in-subset negative case (not run) is `x := make([]int, 2); alias := x[:1]; go write(x); alias[0] = 1`, with a statically known `write` that mutates the overlapping element. The kernel must reject this even with forged permission annotations; rejection must not merely rely on an unsupported closure or foreign feature.

Before prototyping, publish the exact case/mutation inventory and trust ledger. Proposed budget: at most **2,000 non-generated semantic-rule LOC**, locally checked rule/dataflow replay only (no global invariant or proof search), and no new SMT-solver trust. List Go frontend dependencies separately and compare both designs on **the same admitted features**; shrinking the language is not itself a trust reduction.

Reject or narrow the thesis if meaningful positive cases cannot be certified, unsafe variants pass, permissions still depend on trusted hy-check labels, the kernel copies the existing search engine, or added dependencies defeat the trust reduction.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

A restricted-Go semantics, proof format, producer and independent verifier may cost more than they save. Go parsing/type resolution, kernel rules, and the Go compiler/runtime remain trust assumptions. A toy safe subset is not a convincing success.

This certifies neither source equivalence nor business-result correctness, foreign code, or arbitrary Go. Those separate obligations remain. Existing semantics and the native backend must not silently weaken.

If selected, M1 is this written hypothesis and falsification plan; M2 publishes an accept/narrow/reject learning and trust/scope ledger, with illustrative arguments distinguished from experimental evidence. Any execution gets a separately preregistered scope. **No prototype, tests, benchmark or formal safety result has been produced.**

One wildcard winner is selected per cycle. Submission, acknowledgement or a ledger slot is not an award or receivable.

Sources reviewed at the inspected commit: [BOUNTY.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/BOUNTY.md), [MOONSHOT.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/MOONSHOT.md), [GUARANTEES.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/GUARANTEES.md), README, AGENTS, the wildcard template, and the linked related proposals.
